title: Foundry Public Event v1
description: The only event shape Foundry publishes outside the operator's machine, and the only one a visualization consumer such as the Lightning Factory receives. It is deliberately a different schema from the internal event rather than a redacted copy of it: there is no field here that can carry a channel id, a pubkey, a channel point, or a balance, so a forgotten redaction cannot leak one. `additionalProperties` is false at every level for the same reason.

id.description: A random UUIDv4, generated fresh for the public event. NOT a ULID or UUIDv7, which are correct for the internal stream but embed a millisecond timestamp in their leading bits and would publish the exact event time beside a bucket field pretending to hide it. NOT the internal event's id, which would link the public and internal streams.

seq.description: Monotonic per node for the public stream, assigned by the export and independent of the internal seq. Consumers order by seq, never by bucket: buckets are coarse, and rebalance buckets are hourly, so a later event can carry an earlier bucket.

bucket.description: Coarse time bucket, RFC 3339 UTC, floored to the publication granularity (default one minute; always one hour for rebalance events). Not the event's real timestamp: precise timing plus channel state is what makes a public feed useful to an attacker.

node.description: Operator-chosen pseudonym. Never a Lightning pubkey.

type.description: A deliberate subset of the internal vocabulary. Liquidity events are absent entirely: publishing that a channel is depleted, and in which direction, tells a jamming adversary where to strike and a competitor how to price against you. Rebalance events are published, but never attributed to a line and never timed more finely than the hour, because a rebalance happens precisely when a channel was low; see the constraint below and docs/integrations/oogabooga.md.

scale.description: Power-of-ten magnitude in sats instead of an exact amount: dust under 10,000; small 10,000 to 99,999; medium 100,000 to 999,999; large 1,000,000 to 9,999,999; very_large 10,000,000 and up. Measures whatever the event is about: a forward's amount, a channel's capacity, a rebalance's size.

count.description: How many of this event occurred in the bucket. Aggregation is what makes the feed safe to publish and animate.

slot.description: An opaque per-node label so a consumer can animate the same machine consistently within a day. Reassigned every 24 hours at 00:00 UTC and carrying no relationship to any channel id. It is NOT a stable identifier and MUST NOT be treated as one.

allOf.description: Rebalance events are the one place the public feed touches liquidity. A rebalance happens because a channel was depleted, so naming the line would name the depleted channel, precise timing would confirm to a jamming adversary that their attack worked, and a success rate would summarize how often the node failed to find liquidity. All three are therefore impossible to express: no slot, no success_ratio, and an hourly bucket. Holding each hour's rebalances until the hour closes is the export's job; no schema can express emission order.
